text: Answer only the requests the system was built to answer. Every unknown route, method, or action is refused by default, so silence and rejection are the normal state and access is the exception that must be earned.
title: Default Deny

text: Decide every request on its own merits at the moment it arrives. Never let an earlier approval, a familiar address, or a previous session carry trust forward into the next request.
title: Per-Request Authorization

text: Grant each component, window, script, and workflow only the permissions its job requires, and remove every capability that is not exercised. Excess privilege is attack surface waiting for a mistake.
title: Least Privilege

text: Treat every network path as contested, including loopback and the local machine. Location never grants trust: a request that arrives from nearby, from localhost, or from inside the network still has to prove it belongs, because proximity is not identity.
title: Contested Network Assumption

text: Keep a written inventory of what the system actually contains: services, ports, files, identities, and data flows. You cannot protect, categorize, or audit what has never been listed.
title: Resource Inventory

text: Classify each resource by criticality to decide how much control each resource gets: the damage its compromise would cause sets the level of control, logging, and review. Categorization comes before control selection, and uniform treatment wastes effort while leaving the critical parts under-guarded.
title: Categorization by Criticality

text: Place a check in front of every resource and verify that no path reaches it unchecked. A control that covers most entry points leaves the uncovered one as the attacker's door.
title: Enforcement Point Coverage

text: When a resource cannot carry a strong control itself, surround it with compensating ones: strict input bounds, origin validation, rate limits, and logging that together contain what the resource cannot.
title: Compensating Controls

text: Read input with explicit bounds on size, time, and concurrency. Reject oversized and malformed requests early with a clear refusal, and never let one slow or hostile client block the others.
title: Bounded Input Handling

text: Validate the Host header and origin names a request carries before acting on it. Reject unexpected host values so DNS rebinding and name confusion cannot redirect trust to the wrong party.
title: Origin and Host Validation

text: Protection is a loop, not a state: monitor what the system does, assess whether the controls still match the risk, and adjust. Log refusals and failures so the loop has evidence to work from.
title: Monitor and Assess Loop

text: Authorize every release against a written checklist: versions in sync, signatures present and paired, tests green, artifacts complete. Nothing ships on momentum; each release earns its own approval.
title: Release Authorization

text: Scripts and pipelines must stop on the first failed check instead of continuing past it. Verify exit codes, hashes, and health after every step, and treat a missing verification as a failure.
title: Fail-Closed Automation

text: Apply knowledge only where it hardens what the project really contains. Never invent identities, resources, rules, or interfaces to satisfy a model; a control for something that does not exist protects nothing.
title: Tailoring to What Exists
